# COLLATIO: M (Vat. gr. 2125, p. 11) contra S (Schermann 1907)

**Praefatio critica.** Apparatus below is constructed on the three loci as transmitted to me in transcription. I have not myself inspected Vat. gr. 2125, p. 11 codicis ope; the readings of M are therefore reported *ex schedis*, and before the apparatus is set into type the transcription should be re-verified against the manuscript (in particular the spiritus/aspiration of ἥτις and the accentual form χρησμὸς / χρησμός). **All spellings and accents are left exactly as transmitted; no normalisation of ἀπὸ Γαβαών, χρησμὸς, ἐδόθη, etc. has been performed.** No locus here is lacunose: nothing has been lost in the three segments as given, and accordingly no restoration is offered or needed. Where M's text is broken or abbreviated, that must be marked *supra lineam* as (lac.) or (corr.), and no conjecture may be printed in the apparatus as if it were the scribe's text.

**Sigla.**
*S* = Schermann 1907, textus constitutus (lemma text)
*M* = Codex Marchalianus, Vat. gr. 2125, p. 11
*add.* = additio · *om.* = omissio · *subst.* = substitutio · *tr.* = transpositio (translocatio)

---

## Apparatus criticus

**Locus 1**
> ἔχει δὲ εἴσοδον ἀπὸ Γαβαών] ἥτις ἔχει εἴσοδον ἀπὸ Γαβαών *M* ;
> δὲ] ἥτις *M* (*subst.*) ;
> ἔχει *S* ante εἴσοδον] ἔχει *M* post ἥτις (*tr.*) ;

*Classificatio:* **substitutio** (δὲ → ἥτις) cum **transpositione** consequente (ἔχει, quod in *S* secundum locum tenet, in *M* primi membri locum tenet: ἥτις ἔχει). Not a simple addition: δέ is not retained in M. If one prefers a purely mechanical description the variant may be written as *add.* ἥτις *et om.* δέ, but the resulting word order shows a re-writing, not mere interpolation. (Interpretive note only, not a restoration: ἥτις presupposes a feminine antecedent — plausibly a well/cistern term in the preceding sentence of the lemma context; the antecedent itself is not present in the transcribed segment and must be checked in the manuscript before being named.)

**Locus 2**
> ἠρώτων γὰρ οἱ πολέμιοι] ἠρώτων γὰρ οἱ πολέμιοι πόθεν πίνουσιν *M* ;
> πόθεν πίνουσιν *ins. M* post πολέμιοι (*add.*) ;

*Classificatio:* **additio** in fine membri. M supplies the interrogative clause of which ἠρώτων is the verb in *S*; *S*'s phrase is anacoluthic/elliptic without it. Note the plural πίνουσιν (3 pl.), matching οἱ πολέμιοι as subject of an indirect question — orthography and inflection printed as found, not adjusted.

**Locus 3**
> καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς χρησμὸς] ὅτι καὶ χρησμὸς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς *M* ;
> ὅτι *ins. M* ante καί (*add.*) ;
> χρησμὸς] χρησμὸς *M* ante ἐδόθη (*tr.*) ;
> αὐτοῖς] αὐτοῖς *M* post ἐδόθη (*tr.*) ;

*Classificatio:* **additio** (ὅτι) + **transpositio** duorum membrorum (χρησμός advances to the pre-verbal position; αὐτοῖς recedes to the close). The addition of ὅτι converts the asyndetic/paratactic clause of *S* into a subordinate (causal or recitative) clause — formally an addition, functionally a syntactic recasting. The reading ὅτι must not be treated as a dittograph of anything in *S*; *S* has no οὖτ- stem here.

---

## Tabula synoptica classificationum

| Locus | Lemma (*S*) | *M* | Genus variantis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ἔχει δὲ εἴσοδον ἀπὸ Γαβαών | ἥτις ἔχει εἴσοδον ἀπὸ Γαβαών | subst. (δὲ → ἥτις) + tr. (ἔχει) |
| 2 | ἠρώτων γὰρ οἱ πολέμιοι | ἠρώτων γὰρ οἱ πολέμιοι πόθεν πίνουσιν | add. (πόθεν πίνουσιν) |
| 3 | καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς χρησμὸς | ὅτι καὶ χρησμὸς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς | add. (ὅτι) + tr. (χρησμός, αὐτοῖς) |

**Cautio finalis.** None of the three loci is *purely* one class: loci 1 and 3 are compound variants and have been decomposed into their elementary operations above. It would be a false precision to label locus 1 a simple "addition," since δέ does not survive in M; and locus 3 is not a mere "transposition," since ὅτι is new in M. In the printed apparatus the lemma of the base text (*S*) is to be kept as it stands, *sine emendatione*; M's readings enter the apparatus only, never the text.

## Translation

> "And God wrought the sign of Siloam through the prophet: in that, before he died, *ὀλιγωρήσας*, he besought that he might drink water, and straightway [it] was sent to him out of it. Therefore it was called Siloam, which is interpreted 'Sent'…
> **[text broken — lacuna indicated by the ellipsis in the transcription]**
> If, then, the Jews came, the water came forth; but if foreigners (ἀλλόφυλοι), it did not. Wherefore even unto this day it comes forth suddenly, that the mystery may be made manifest."

---

## Philological notes

**1. Provenance.** The ascription to Codex Marchalianus (Vat. gr. 2125, saec. VI, the great prophet-book with Hexaplaric and Coptic–Arabic marginal glosses) cannot be verified from the transcription alone. Marchalianus is a codex of the prophets with apparatus; a Marian/hagiographic notice of this type would occur, if at all, in a marginal scholion. The citation should be treated as unattributed until the folio is collated *ex codice*. The etymologizing form (Siloam = ἀπεσταλμένος, cf. Jo. 9:7) and the *historiola* of the water granted to the dying prophet are, however, characteristic of Graeco-Jewish exegetical tradition attached to Is. 8:6 (τὸ ὕδωρ τοῦ Σιλωαμ).

**2. `ὀλιγωρήσας`.** Retained exactly as transcribed. The verb ὀλιγωρέω means "to hold in slight esteem, to disregard," which yields no tolerable sense with ηὔξατο πιεῖν ὕδωρ. It is likely a scribal anomaly (perhaps for *ὀλιγωρήσας* standing as a corruption of a fatigue-/thirst-word, e.g. *ὀλιγοψυχήσας*, *ὀλιγωρῶν* in the sense 'in low case', or *διψήσας*). I have therefore left it untranslated within the sentence rather than import a conjectural sense. The sense required by the narrative is evidently 'in his extremity / fainting', but this is an inference, **not** the reading of the text.

**3. `ἀπεστάλη αὐτῷ ἐξ αὐτοῦ`.** No subject is expressed. Supplying "[water]" (or the implied fem. *πηγή*, sc. ἀπεστάλη αὐτῷ ἐξ αὐτῆς) is conjectural; the bracketed element in the translation marks this. The antecedent of both pronouns is likewise left indefinite by the Greek: `αὐτοῦ` may construe with τοῦ Σιλωὰμ / τοῦ τόπου rather than with ὕδωρ.

**4. `ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται ἀπεσταλμένος`.** The masc. participle is attached to a noun (Σιλωάμ) that is construed elsewhere in the sentence with τὸ σημεῖον (ntr.); the grammatical inconcinnity is preserved, not normalised. The etymology presupposes Heb. שִׁלֹחַ < שׁלח, "to send."

**5. `ἐὰν … ἤρχοντο … ἐξήρχετο … ἐὰν δὲ … οὔ`.** An irregular (mixed) conditional: protasis with ἐάν + imperfect, apodosis imperfect. I have rendered the iterative/past-referring force ("would come forth / came forth") without converting the Greek into a classical future-less-vivid. `οὔ` stands absolutely in place of a verbal clause (cf. the elliptic καὶ ὅς, "and not") and is so represented.

**6. `ἀλλόφυλοι`.** Translated "foreigners," retaining the Greek in parentheses: in LXX usage the word is the standing equivalent of פְּלִשְׁתִּים ("Philistines"), whereas here it appears to be used in the later generalised sense of 'non-Jews / peoples of another stock'. Both values remain possible from the Greek alone; I have not resolved the ambiguity.

**7. Lacuna.** The sentence after `ἀπεσταλμένος` is broken in the transcription. The connecting matter between the etymology and the conditional clause is **not present** and is **not** supplied here. Any restoration of the lost words (e.g. a clause on the periodic movement of the spring, or an explicit identification of the prophet) would be conjecture and is not offered as text.

**8. `αἰφνιδίως ἐξέρχεται … ἵνα δειχθῇ τὸ μυστήριον`.** The presential `ἐξέρχεται` ("comes forth") with ἕως σήμερον is rendered in the present, matching the Greek. `τὸ μυστήριον` is left as "the mystery" (not 'sacrament' or 'type'): the referent is undefined in the surviving text, and given the lacuna it cannot be determined whether the μυστήριον is the prefiguration of baptism, of the water from Christ's side, or of the election of Israel.

# Collatio: Vat. lat. 629, f. 3v (V) contra Chaparro Gómez 1985 (C), Isidore §37

**Praefatio methodologica.** Lemma = textus base C; lectio manuscripti sequitur, siglo **V** addito. Orthographia (etiam scribarum menda) *non* normalizatur: retineo **extincxit** (C), **extinxit** (V), **Hic** cum capitali, **atroque**, **nobilis** / **nobili** prout transscripta sunt. Nulla lacuna in tribus locis collatis indicatur; segmenta integra sunt nec quicquam supplendum propono (cf. adnot. ad 2c–d).

---

## Apparatus criticus

### Locus 1 — *ille enim ex numero pastorum fuit*

[ille] Hic V ; **substitutio** (pron. demonstr. *ille* → *hic*; discessus deicticus, non mere orthographicus).
[ille] Hic V ; **orthographicum** (littera initialis *H* maiuscula in V; orthotypographicum scribendi, sine vi grammatica).

*(reliqua verba —* enim, ex, numero, pastorum, fuit *— consentiunt.)*

### Locus 2 — *hic genere nobilis ortus in Hierusalem*

[hic] Hic autem V ; **additio** (coniunctivi *autem* inserti a V); simul **orthographicum** (*H* maiuscula, cf. loc. 1).
[nobilis] nobili V ; **substitutio** (mutatio flexionis: *nobilis* nom./gen. — C : *nobili* abl. — V, quod cum *genere* aptius congruit); fieri tamen potest ut sit **orthographicum** (amissio *-s* finalis, s-mobile). Utraque analysin propono, neutram ut certam.
[in] om. V ; **omissio** (praepositio *in* ante *Hierusalem* in V deest).
[ortus] ortus est V ; **additio** (copulae *est* insertae a V post participium).
 *Analytis alternativa:* [in] est V ; **substitutio** (*in* → *est*). Haec quoque legi potest; propter ordinem verborum (*ortus est Hierusalem*) tamen separatio in omissionem + additionem mihi probabilior videtur, minime certa.

*(reliqua verba —* genere, ortus, Hierusalem *— consentiunt; orthographia Hierusalem in utroque eadem.)*

### Locus 3 — *atrocique supplicio excruciatum extincxit*

[atrocique] atroque V ; **orthographicum** (haplologia / syncopa *-ic-* : *atrocique* → *atroque*; formam *atro* tamen ut abl. syncopatum ipsius *ater* veteres quoque admittunt — ideo non ausim id mere mendum scribale vocare). Si formam distinctam esse mavis: **substitutio** (flexionis / thematis).
[extincxit] extinxit V ; **orthographicum** (in C geminatio insolens *-ccx-*, per analogiam *-nxi* orta; in V forma simplicior *-nx-*). Lemma ipsum retineo sic ut C transscribit, **extincxit**, non normalizando ad *extinxit*.

*(reliqua verba —* supplicio, excruciatum *— consentiunt.)*

---

## Conspectus classificationum

| Locus | Lemma (C) | Lectio (V) | Classificatio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ille | Hic | substitutio (+ orthogr. capitalis) |
| 2 | hic | Hic autem | additio (*autem*) |
| 2 | nobilis | nobili | substitutio flexionis (possibiliter orthographicum) |
| 2 | in | *om.* | omissio |
| 2 | ortus | ortus est | additio (*est*) |
| 3 | atrocique | atroque | orthographicum (haplologia) |
| 3 | extincxit | extinxit | orthographicum (geminatio consonantis) |

**Numerus variantium:** 7 (ex quibus 2 substantivae — substitutio pronominis in loc. 1, mutatio flexionis in loc. 2 — ceterae aut particulae insertae/deletae aut orthographicae). Textus in V huius paragraphi nihil lacunosum continet; nihil supplendum nec restituendum propono.

## Text (as transmitted — no normalization)

'Tradunt autem Hebraei duabus ex causis interfectum fuisse Esaiam : unum, quod eos appellauerit principes Sodomorum et populum Gomorrae ; alterum, quod, testante Domino ad Moysen « non poteris uidere faciem meam », iste ausus est exclamare : « Vidi Dominum sedentem super thronum excelsum... », non arbitrantes caecati mente Iudaei quod in sequentibus faciem et pedes Dei Seraphin texisse narrauerat ac media tantum eius uidisse scribat. Iacet sub quercu Rogel iuxta decursus aquarum.'

**Lacunae:** none marked in the codex. The three points after 'excelsum' represent abbreviation (truncation) of the biblical citation in the transcription, not a physical defect of f. 3v; the passage that the scribe leaves unquoted is Isa. 6.2 (the *Seraphim* who veil face and feet). No conjectural supplement is offered here.

## Translation

'The Hebrews report, moreover, that Esaias was put to death for two reasons: the one — that he had called them "the princes of Sodom and the people of Gomorrah"; the other — that, the Lord bearing witness to Moses "you shall not be able to see my face", this man dared to cry aloud "I saw the Lord sitting upon a high throne…" — the Jews, blinded in mind, not considering that in the sequel he had narrated that the Seraphim covered the face and the feet of God and that he saw only the middle portion of Him, he sets down in writing. He lies beneath the oak of Rogel, beside the outflowings of the waters.'

## Philological notes (anomalies preserved, not emended)

1. **Esaiam** (not *Isaiam*); the spelling is transmitted and left untouched.
2. **unum … alterum** in place of the expected feminine agreeing with *causis*: transmitted as written; the construction is apparently an accusative of the thing stated (Gk. accusative), but the genderal incongruity is a scribal anomaly, not to be regularized to *unam … alteram*.
3. **appellauerit** (perfect subjunctive) in the causal *quod*-clause; retained as transmitted.
4. **principes Sodomorum et populum Gomorrae** — Isa. 1.10 adapted into accusative government after *appellauerit*; the Vulgate has the vocative *popule Gomorrae*. The transmitted *populum* is not to be silently conformed.
5. **« non poteris uidere faciem meam »** — Exod. 33.20 (Vulgate agrees word for word); cited as the Lord's testimony *ad Moysen*.
6. **« Vidi Dominum sedentem super thronum excelsum... »** — Isa. 6.1. The wording *super thronum excelsum* reflects the Old Latin/Greek (LXX καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ), not the Vulgate *super solio excelso et elevato*. This text is quoted exactly as it stands, truncation and all.
7. **Seraphin** — Hebraizing declension preserved (Vulgate *Seraphim*); **texisse** is the author's paraphrase for the biblical *velabant*.
8. **narrauerat … scribat** — a marked tense/hood shift (perfect indicative against present subjunctive) within one *quod*-clause, whose subject is the prophet himself; the anacoluthon is left untranslated-by-reconstruction and merely rendered literally ("he had narrated … he sets down in writing"). It is not corrected to *narrauerit … scribat*.
9. **caecati mente Iudaei** — perfect passive participle in the nominative plural, separated from its noun by *mente*; the ablative of respect is rendered "blinded in mind".
10. **media tantum eius** — neuter plural used substantivally for *media pars*, i.e. the middle of the divine body left exposed between the veiled face and feet (cf. Isa. 6.2).
11. **sub quercu Rogel iuxta decursus aquarum** — "the oak of Rogel": the biblical locus is a *fons* / *lapis* Rogel (1 Reg. 1.9; 2 Reg. 17.17), and *quercu* appears to be an anomalous assimilation to the tree of the prophet's martyrdom (sawn asunder "under a tree"); *decursus aquarum* is a biblical-coloured expression for the outflow of waters. Both words are transmitted as written and are not reconciled with the biblical nomenclature.

# COLLATION OF THE DREAM-REPORT FRAGMENTS
## 4Q530 2 ii:4 ‖ 6Q8 1:1–2 ‖ 4Q531 1:6

---

## 0. Methodological statement (to be read first)

Only the three transcriptions as supplied are collated. I treat them as data, not as texts to be improved.

1. **Ellipses in the supplied transcription of 6Q8 1:1–2 are physical lacunae** (or, at minimum, unresolved gaps in the transmission of the line). They are written below as `[…]`. **I supply no restoration into them**, and no hypothetical supplement in this apparatus may be cited as the reading of the manuscript.
2. **Scribal orthography is not normalised.** `אוהיא`, `באראכאל`, `ואשתעיו`, `נפיליא`, `אבוי`, `לה` stand exactly as transmitted. Where a normalised or usual form exists (`אוהי`, `ברכאל`, `ליה`), it appears only in a note, never in the *textus*.
3. **These three passages are not variants of one another.** They are three different scenes of the same literary work (4Q530 = collective frame; 6Q8 and 4Q531 = individual speeches inside such a frame). Consequently, in the apparatus below, absence of a name is marked **non extat in loco**, not *om.* (nothing has been omitted by the scribe of that locus — the word simply never belonged there).
4. Where a prosopographic or tradition-historical identification is **inferred**, it is flagged as inference and never as a reading.

**Sigla used:** `4Q530`, `4Q531`, `6Q8` (numerical sigla only). The designations `EnGiants` *a/b/c* vary from edition to edition and are **not used here**. Editions to be consulted for verification: J. T. Milik's plates and copies for the Cave 4 Aramaic parabiblical material (cf. also his *The Books of Enoch*, Oxford 1976, for the Enochic context); L. T. Stuckenbruck, *The Book of Giants from Qumran* (TSAJ 63, Tübingen 1997) for the standard collected edition. *I do not certify here the DJD volume number in which 4Q530–4Q531 were published; this must be verified before formal citation.*

---

## 1. The three loci, unaltered

| Siglum | Transcription (verbatim) |
|---|---|
| **4Q530** 2 ii:4 | `ואשתעיו חלמיהון בקהל חבריהון נפיליא` |
| **6Q8** 1:1–2 | `ואמר לאוהיא […] אחי […] באראכאל אבוי הוה עמי` |
| **4Q531** 1:6 | `ואדין אמר אוהיא לה אנס עלי חלם` |

---

## 2. (a) Speakers, addressees, and roles

| | 4Q530 2 ii:4 | 6Q8 1:1–2 | 4Q531 1:6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Grammatical subject of the frame** | 3cp (`ואשתעיו`), subject unexpressed, implicit | 3ms (`ואמר`), historical imperfect, name **not extant** | 3ms (`אמר`), perfect, named: `אוהיא` |
| **Addressee** | the collective: `קהל חבריהון נפיליא` | `לאוהיא` (+ `אחי`, function uncertain — see below) | `לה`, 3ms suffixed preposition; person **not named in the extant text** |
| **Discourse mode** | narrator's report of a collective act (no direct speech) | direct speech within a narrative frame | direct speech introduced by `ואדין` |
| **Role of speaker(s)** | the dreamers as a body among their own class (the Nephilim), reporting **publicly, in assembly** (`קהל`) | a single dreamer recounting a dream-scene in which a father-figure appears (`הוה עמי`) | an involuntary visionary: the dream is *imposed*, not sought |
| **Identification** | anonymous (plural) | **name non extat**; prosopographic inference only (see below) | `אוהיא` — reading, not inference |

### Notes on roles

**4Q530.** The subject of `ואשתעיו` is not expressed; it is recoverable only from the apposition `חבריהון נפיליא` — "their companions, the Nephilim." Note the syntax carefully: `חבריהון` is a 3mp suffixed noun, i.e. the audience are the companions **of the speakers**; the apposition `נפיליא` designates *that same audience* as belonging to the class of the Nephilim. The speakers are therefore **a subset of the Nephilim** (the dreamers), and the hearers are their fellows in `קהל` (assembly/council). This is a frame-report (*Rahmenbericht*), not a speech: it sets the genre-scene in which the individual speeches of 6Q8 and 4Q531 are to be imagined.

**6Q8.** The speaker's name is **not extant**. What survives is (i) the addressee `אוהיא`; (ii) the word `אחי`; (iii) the patronymic `ברכאל אבוי`. Two philological problems must be registered and left open:

* `אחי` stands between two lacunae, so its syntactic function cannot be established. It is either (a) a suffixed noun in vocative force, "my brother," addressed to `אוהיא`; or (b) part of a phrase now lost. If (a) is taken literally (kinship), the speaker would be `אוהיא`'s brother — a figure otherwise known in the tradition under a different name; if (b) or if the term is conventional ("comrade"), no kinship is implied. **The word cannot be made to decide the matter.**
* **`אבוי` is a 3ms suffixed form, "his father."** The translation "Barakel **my** father" supplied in the request presupposes a 1cs suffix (`אבי` or the like), which is **not the transmitted reading**. Either the translation is free, or the speaker refers to his own father in the third person, or the suffix points to a third party mentioned in the lacuna. **This is an unresolved discrepancy and must not be harmonised in the text.**

That said, the patronymic `ברכאל` does allow a *prosopographic* inference (not a reading): elsewhere in the Book of Giants tradition a dreamer is named with Barakel as father. The identification of the 6Q8 speaker with that dreamer is therefore **probable but inferential**, and his name must be marked `non extat` in any apparatus of these three loci.

**4Q531.** `אוהיא` is the speaker and is named; the addressee `לה` is not. The idiom `אנס עלי חלם` (see §3) characterises him as an **involuntary recipient** — the dream is forced upon him — which is precisely the register of ominous, doom-bearing revelation. Within the collated material `אוהיא` is thus the only figure who is **both addressee (6Q8) and speaker (4Q531)**: he is the pivot between the individual dream-report and the assembled body of 4Q530. His status as a leading figure among the giants (traditionally one of a pair of brothers) is **tradition-historical background, not established by these three lines**.

**Composite role-list produced by these loci:**

| Figure | Roles attested *in these loci* | Roles in the wider tradition (background only) |
|---|---|---|
| `אוהיא` | addressee; speaker; involuntary dreamer | chief giant; dreamer; petitioner to Enoch |
| unnamed speaker of 6Q8 | speaker; dream-narrator; son ("his/my father" — unresolved) of `ברכאל` | probably the dreamer-emissary who flies to Enoch |
| `ברכאל` | father-figure *within the dream-scene* (`הוה עמי` "was with me") | progenitor in the giant genealogy |
| `נפיליא` | collective class: audience and co-companions of the dreamers | the doomed race |
| Mahway | **not named in any of the three loci** | dreamer; envoy |
| Gilgamesh | **not named in any of the three loci** | giant warrior hero; see the caution in §4 |

## 3. (b) The common formula for dream narration

The three fragments preserve **two formal members of one and the same report-scheme**. Neither member alone constitutes "the formula"; the formula is the composite pattern.

### Member I — the collective frame (4Q530 2 ii:4)

```
[√שׂע hitp. + חלמ + 3mp suffix]  +  [ב + קהל + 3mp suff. noun + class name]
   ואשתעיו  חלמיהון                 בקהל  חבריהון   נפיליא
```

### Member II — the individual report (4Q531 1:6; partially 6Q8 1:1–2)

```
[discourse marker + אמר + PN + dative]  +  [involuntariness idiom]  +  [dream-scene, 1cs]
   ואדין   אמר  אוהיא  לה               אנס  עלי חלם                 (non extat here)
   ואמר   לאוהיא  [… א]חי […           …                              הוה עמי
```

### Formal correspondences (the "common" core)

| Element | 4Q530 2 ii:4 | 6Q8 1:1–2 | 4Q531 1:6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Report-verb** | `ואשתעיו` (√שׂע hitp., 3cp perf., plene ending `-יו`) | non extat (lacuna) | non extat |
| **B. Object noun `חלום`** | `חלמיהון` (pl. + 3mp suff.) | **non extat in the surviving text** | `לם` of `חלום` — `אנס עלי חלם` (sg.) |
| **C. Speech-introduction** | implicit in the narrative plural | `ואמר` (imperf.) + nominal addressee `לאוהיא` | `ואדין` + `אמר` (perf.) + pronominal addressee `לה` |
| **D. Addressee-sociative** | `בקהל חבריהון נפיליא` (class + assembly) | `לאוהיא … אחי` (individual + kinship term) | `לה` (bare pronoun) |
| **E. Experiencer suffix, 1cs** | — | `עמי` ("with me") | `עלי` ("upon me") |
| **F. Involuntariness idiom** | non extat | non extat (lacuna) | `אנס עלי חלם` |
| **Tense of the frame** | 3cp **perfect** | 3ms **imperfect** → `הוה` | 3ms **perfect** |

### The composite type-formula (an editorial abstraction — **this is not a manuscript text**)

> `ואדין אמר PN₁ (ל + PN₂ / ל-הּ) [אחי] …` — `ואשתעיו חלמיהון בקהל חבריהון נפיליא` — `אנס עלי חלם` / `… הוה עמי` — [dream-scene, 1cs, e.g. `חזית` …]

Two lexical constants hold the scheme together: the noun **`חלום`/`חלמיהון`** (present in 4Q530 and 4Q531; **not extant in 6Q8 as transcribed**), and the **1cs experiencer marker** (`עמי`, `עלי`) in the two speech-fragments. The addressee is always defined socially — class (`נפיליא`), kinship (`אחי`), or person (`אוהיא`) — never left bare.

### Remarks on Member II, `אנס עלי חלם`

The gloss "a dream has been forced upon me" is defensible, but the morphology is ambiguous and **must not be decided in the text**:

1. `אנס` = Peal 3ms perfect of √אנס "to compel": "a dream has compelled/forced [itself] upon me" (`חלום` as subject, verb-first order);
2. `אנס` as a predicative/adverbial notion "unbidden, against my will": "unbidden there [was] upon me a dream."

`עלי` is unambiguously 1cs ("upon me"), and the gloss is consistent with it. Compare, for the *concept* (not for the wording), the Aramaic biblical idiom of the dream that imposes itself on the dreamer; **no verbal identity with any biblical passage is claimed here**.

The passage must be translated **as it stands in the transcription supplied**, but three things have to be said before any rendering can be offered.

**(a) The transcription is not a diplomatic copy.** It reproduces an *edition*: the square brackets enclose **editorial supplements** (words printed by an editor but not preserved on the skin), and the "[. . .]" within brackets marks **physical loss**. ## 3. Translation

> "[. . .] **L1** Thereupon the two of them dreamed dreams, and the sleep of their eyes fled from them, and they rose and they came [. . .] **L2** — and they recounted their dreams in the assembly of [**their companions**] the giants:
>
> 'In my dream I was seeing during this night — **L3** [and behold, a garden . . .] *gardens / bowers* (גננין, sense uncertain), and there were . . . irrigating . . . **L4** [. . . *two hundred trees*, and there came forth] great roots from their stumps **L5** [. . .]; all the waters, and a fire that burned in all [. . . the garden . . .] **L6** [. . .]'"

Notes on the rendering:

* **נדת מנהון** is given as "fled from them" on the analogy of Est. 6:1; if the scribe intended a by-form of נפל the sense is "fell from them," i.e. "were shaken off from them." Either way the idiom denotes a sudden waking. The choice between the two is *not* philologically demonstrable from the preserved letters.
* **[חבריהון]** is printed by the editor between "the assembly of" and "the giants"; the resulting construct chain ("the assembly of [their companions,] the giants") is syntactically strained, which is itself an argument against treating the supplement as secure. It is presumably taken from the parallel in the Manichaean witness ("in the presence of their friends").
* **גננין** is left untranslated-in-part: the grammar (a noun or adjective following גנתא and preceding והוו משקין) is clear, the lexeme is not.
* **מִנָּא**? — no such form occurs; **כול מיא** = "all the waters"; the verb governing "the waters" may lie in **L5**, in which case "all the waters and the fire which burned" could be the *object* of a lost verb (e.g. "…consumed…"), or could be the *subject* of a lost clause. The preserved syntax is incomplete; I do not supply an ending.
* "[*two hundred trees*]" is set off above precisely because it is *not* preserved. Any interpretation built on the number 200 rests on a conjecture.

## 4. Symbolic sense of the garden, trees, water and fire

What follows is **interpretation**, not translation. In a fragment cut away at exactly this point, symbolism can be established only typologically, by comparison with the biblical and parabiblical use of the same images. Degrees of confidence are marked.

### The garden (גנתא)
Lexically גן/גנה is the **enclosed, planted, irrigated** space — orchard, park, *paradeisos* (cf. Neh 2:8; Eccl 2:5; Song 4:13) — set over against the unwatered steppe. Paradigmatically it is Eden (Gen 2:8–15), "the garden of God" of Ezek 28:13; 31:8–9, and the "garden of the LORD" of Gen 13:10; Isa 51:3.

Symbolically it denotes **an ordered, walled, well-watered domain of life and fruitfulness** — the habitable world in its divinely given order and productivity, "planted" and hence under care. In the giants-tradition, where the earth has been invaded and filled with violence by the offspring of the Watchers (Gen 6:1–4; 1 En 7–10), such a garden is most naturally the **world as the sphere of the giants' growth and dominion**, still clothed in Edenic-looking prosperity while actually under doom. A second possibility is that the garden is more narrowly the giants' own encampment or progeny.

A very close typological parallel for the whole scene is **Gen 13:10–13 + 19:24–25**: the Jordan valley is "like the garden of the LORD" immediately before Sodom is consumed with fire from heaven. Garden-likeness preceding fiery destruction is thus an inherited biblical schema, and this vision appears to reproduce it.

### The trees (אילנין) and their roots (שרשין רברבין מן עקרהון)
Trees are, in prophetic and apocalyptic symbolism, **living beings — kings, empires, peoples** (Ezek 31:2–18, where the cedar is Pharaoh and the cypresses, plane trees and "all the trees of Eden" are the nations under him; Dan 4, where Nebuchadnezzar is the world-tree watered by heaven's dew; 1 En 83–84, where trees figure the peoples and the sinners to be destroyed and the righteous to be planted; 4 Ezra 4:24–27). Applied here, the trees are most plausibly **the giants themselves and their breed** — their enormous stature corresponding to the monstrous growth of Ezekiel's cedar and to the "gigantic height" of 1 En 7:2. If the restored numeral "two hundred" were genuine, it would most likely allude to the **two hundred Watchers** of 1 En 6:6; Jub. 5:6 — but since that numeral is *supplied by the editor*, the identification must remain a conjecture built on a conjecture.

The trees are cut down (only stumps, עקר, remain: cf. Dan 4:12, 15), yet **great roots go forth from their stumps**. Two readings are possible and the broken text cannot decide between them:

1. **Renewal from a judged stock** — the biblical "stump" hope: Job 14:7–9 ("there is hope for a tree… at the scent of water it will put forth shoots"); Isa 11:1 (a shoot from the stump of Jesse); Isa 6:13 ("the holy seed is its stump"); Dan 4:12–15 (the stump is preserved and revives).
2. **Persistence of the evil brood** — the giant survives his own destruction in another form. This has a precise parallel in 1 En 15:8–12 and Jub. 10:1–14, where the **evil spirits proceed from the giants** after their flesh has perished: the tree is felled, but its roots still throw up a growth. Given that this is a giants-text, and that the roots are called "great" (רברבין, the same epithet applied to giant-power elsewhere), this second sense is the more probable of the two.

### The water (מיא; והוו משקין)
Water has a **deliberate double valence**, and the lacunae prevent our eliminating either half:

* **Water as the source of the overgrowth.** The garden is irrigated (והוו משקין); cf. Gen 2:6, 10; Ps 104:16; and above all **Ezek 31:4–7**, where the deep and its rivers make the cedar grow until "all the trees of Eden" envy it. Water is thus what nourishes the giants' excessive growth.
* **Water as judgment.** "All the waters" appearing together with fire points to the **waters of the Flood**, the standard instrument of the first cosmic judgment (Gen 6–8; 1 En 10:13, 22; Jub. 5:22; 2 Pet 3:6). Compare also Dan 7:2–3, the beast stirred up from the great sea by the four winds.

Both may be intended: the same waters that make the trees enormous are the waters that drown them (note Ezek 31:14–15, the well-watered cedar going down to Sheol "with those nourished by the waters"). I would not assert more than this.

### The fire (נורא דלקת)
Fire here is **divine judgment, the consuming agent of the world-garden**. The parallels converge: the fire and brimstone that consumes the "garden of the LORD" of the Jordan plain (Gen 19:24–25, with 13:10); Isa 66:15–16 ("by fire will the LORD plead"); Zeph 3:8 ("the whole earth shall be devoured by the fire of my jealousy"); **Mal 3:19/4:1**, "it shall leave them **neither root nor branch**" — language remarkably apt beside a vision of felled trees and shooting roots; 2 Pet 3:7 (the world "reserved unto fire against the day of judgment"); and, in Enochic tradition, the fiery abyss prepared for the fallen Watchers (1 En 14:19; 21:7–10).

A second, less exclusive possibility is the **fire of the divine Presence or of divine self-execution** against a semi-divine intruder in Eden — note **Ezek 28:18**, where the guardian cherub in the garden of God is destroyed "by fire from the midst of thee." Garden + superhuman being + fire is precisely that configuration.

### Summary of the symbolism
Garden = the well-ordered, watered, life-bearing world (paradisiacal in appearance) which is at the same time the domain of the giants; trees = the giants and their offspring, luxuriantly grown; water = the source of that monstrous growth and/or the flood-waters of judgment; fire = the consuming divine judgment by which the whole garden is to be burnt. The rising of great roots from the felled stumps signals either a hope of renewal or — more probably in this tradition — the survival of the giant-evil in demonic form after the destruction of the bodies.

## 5. What cannot be said

The fragment is broken at the decisive points, and I therefore do **not** determine: (i) which of the two dreamers is speaking (their names, if they stood here, are lost in **L1–L2**); (ii) how many trees there were — "two hundred" is an editorial restoration; (iii) whether the water is here nourishing, destructive, or both, since the governing verb is lost in **L5**; (iv) what the fire finally did to the trees and the garden, the column ending mid-clause in **L6**; (v) the dream's interpretation, which in this genre follows the report and which would alone convert the above symbolism from *inference* into *evidence*. No restoration of these gaps can be presented as certain, and none has been so presented here.
